div.head: Wi 11
div.ab: gif friman þonne an ðane forbodenan timan, sio he healsfange scyldig; ⁊ se man se þæt arasie, he age healf þæt wite ⁊ ðæt weorc.
Gif friman þonne an ðane forbodenan timan, sio he healsfange scyldig; ⁊ se man se þæt arasie, he age healf þæt wite ⁊ ðæt weorc.
Gif friman þonne an ðane forbodenan timan, sio he healsfange scyldig, ⁊ se man se þæt arasie, he age healf þæt wite ⁊ ðæt weorc.

Wenn ein Freier aber in der verbotenen Zeit [arbeitet], sei er Halsfang [dem Könige] schuldig; und der Mann, welcher das ertappt, er erhalte zur Hälfte das Strafgeld und den Arbeit[sertrag, den jener verliert].

But if a freeman [works] in the forbidden time, let him be liable for his healsfang [to the king]; and the man who catches him at it, let him receive half the fine and the [proceeds of the] work [which the other loses].
If a freeman works during the forbidden time, he shall forfeit his healsfang, and the man who informs against him shall have half the fine, and [the profits arising from] the labour.
If, however, a freeman [works] in the forbidden time, he is to be liable to his healsfang; and the man who discovers it is to have half the fine and half the [profit from the] work.
If, however, a freeman [works] in that forbidden time, let him be liable for healsfang, and the man who detects that, he shall own half that fine and/or that work.

note.seg: þane später ac. sg.; man bessere die Übs.: ‘jener’
þane is a later acc. sg.; the translation should be corrected to: ‘jener’
Keine Textlücke, sondern Ellipse (s. d. Wb 12, wohin n. 5 zu versetzen) des Stiles, zu ergänzen aus deð in 10. Ebenso u. 21
Not a lacuna in the text but a stylistic ellipsis (see that word in Wb 12, to which n. 5 is to be transferred), to be supplied from deð in 10. Likewise below 21
Instrumental, von scyldig (s. d. Wb 4a) abhängend. — Vgl. Gl Halsfang 6f
Instrumental, dependent on scyldig (see that word in Wb 4a). — Cf. Gl Halsfang 6f
S. Wb Relativum A I a. — Halbes Strafgeld erhält der Anzeiger auch u. 26. — Arasod für ‘deprehensus auf Verbrechen’ Wærferth Gregor 27
See Wb Relativum A I a. — The informer also receives half the fine below 26. — Arasod for ‘deprehensus in a crime’ Wærferth Gregor 27

Ebenso verliert, ausser Strafgeld, das Erhandelte der Sonntagskäufer; EGu 7. Wilkins änderte stillschweigend þæt were mit zwei grammatischen Fehlern; þone were empfiehlt auch Schmid. Allein Wergeld [des Täters] wäre, als Halsfang vervielfachend, für diesen zu hohe Strafe und viel zu hoch für die Anzeige; s. d. Gl 1. 3

Likewise the Sunday purchaser loses, besides the fine, what he has bought; EGu 7. Wilkins silently emended to þæt were, with two grammatical errors; Schmid too recommends þone were. But wergild [of the offender], being a multiple of the healsfang, would be too heavy a punishment for him and much too high for the denunciation; see that word in Gl 1. 3

healsfang is the name given, apparently, to the first instalment of the wergeld—a sum which is to be paid only to the nearest relatives (see Be Wergilde, cap. 4 and 5). In Kent the payment to be made before the grave is closed (see Abt. cap. 22) is probably to be regarded as healsfang. The origin of the term is uncertain, but the Norse halsfang (‘embrace’) suggests the possibility that this payment denoted the re-establishment of peace between the families involved in the vendetta. On the other hand, cap. 12 f. below would seem rather to favour the idea that it was a redemption from imprisonment (enslavement).

note.label: healsfang
note.seg: A proportion of the wergild which went to the nearest relatives of the slain man. When the wergild was 1200 shillings it was 120 shillings, and it may be that this ratio applies to other wergilds.

note.label: healsfang,
note.seg: This probably means ‘fine in lieu of imprisonment,’ and likely represents 20 per cent of the wergild, that is, 20 shillings for a freeman. (See discussion under ‘Transgressing the laws of the church’ in Commentary).

note.label: work.
note.seg: ⁊ can represent ‘and’ or ‘or’; in the next two clauses it is almost certainly adversative. See note i to §9.
